To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
valvular tissue consists of a matrix of collagen, elastic fibers, proteoglycans, and glycoproteins, and a cellular component of interstitial cells and endocardial endothelium.
valvular matrix is secreted by valvular interstital cells and that these cells are contractile and communicate with each other.
valvular matrix is synthesized and secreted by valvular intersttitial cells, which have some of the properties of smooth-muscular cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function, and the regulation of valvular matrix synthesis by valvular interstial cells.
the structure, regulation, and function of the valvular interstitium.
understanding how cardiac valve structure and function are regulated by valvular interstital cells and their interactions with the matrix and endothelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure and function, and hence the role of the interstitial cell in the normal and diseased heart valves is not yet well defined.
the interstitial cells are the key cells in the regulation and control of the structure and functions of the cardiac valves.
the interstitial cell is the most interesting and important cell type in the heart valve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
valvular matrix cells are a heterogeneous cell population that are contractile, secrete matrix proteins, and communicate with each other.
the cardiac valve interstitial cell is the key regulator of valve structure.
valvular cells are contractile and have smooth muscle-like characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
valvular disease can be prevented and/or reversed by understanding the molecular biology of valvular cells.
the valvular interstital cell is a complex, dynamic, and heterogeneous cell type that regulates the function and structure of the cardiac valve.
the valve is a dynamic structure and that valvular cells are capable of remodeling in response to injury.
